```

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified then the current text window is deactivated, preventing any received raw text from being displayed in that window. Switching to another text window data table entry can re-enable text displaying if that other window is "activated". _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to disable more than one text window in the same `$DTW$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: If a slot (0-35) is specified then that text window slot is deactivated. This may or may not affect the current status of received text. If the slot specified just happens to be the current slot then all received text is deactivated. If the text window slot isn't the current text window then that text window is deactivated, but what is done with received raw text depends on the status of the current text window's status. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: You may specify "CUR" to explicitly deactivate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: You may also specify a slot of "ALL" to deactivate all defined text window slots. Text window data table entries that are not defined, or that are protected are not affected by this operation. This would also deactivate any raw text that is received because the act of deactivating all windows will consequently deactivate the current one too. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: If the text window being deactivated is protected, then it is not changed (ie, deactivated). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: This command is useful in Host Commands when you click on a Mouse Field, it would halt any further output to the text window.

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$DTW$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $DTW$
requirements.text: _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8726 `rv_disable`); corpus (14 uses)._

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: _Erase Text Window_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$ETW(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text:
```text
$ETW(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
         ───────
         ALL
         CUR
         0-35
         ───────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: If no parameter(s) are specified then the current text window in use is cleared. If you specify a slot from 0-35 then the corresponding text window slot is erased. You may also specify "ALL" to erase all currently defined text window slots. Finally, you may specify the value of "CUR" to also indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: It should be noted that the entire text window's bounding rectangle is erased, not just the display region inside the bounding rectangle. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to erase more than one text window in the same `$ETW$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: If any text window specified aren't defined, or if the viewport is deactivated, then this command does nothing for that viewport parameter. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: This command is useful in Host Commands when you click on a Mouse Field, it could erase the text window THEN transmit the remainder of the Host Command (if any).

requirements.heading: $ETW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$ETW(ALL)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: _Is text window an extended text window?_

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A4._

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$ISEXTWIN(windowno)$`

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text:
```text
$ISEXTWIN(opt:WINDOWNO)$
              ────────
              CUR
              0-35
              ────────
          def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: This text variable determines if the specified text window is an extended text window or not. If the WINDOWNO parameter is omitted, then it will inquire about the current text window. If WINDOWNO is specified, then it must be the value "CUR" for the current text window, or a window data table entry number from 0-35 to inquire about a specific text window data table entry.

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: If the specified text window is not defined, or deactivated, then this text variable returns a value of "-1". If it is an extended text window, then a "1" is returned, otherwise a "0" is returned to indicate that it is a standard (non-extended) text window.

requirements.heading: $ISEXTWIN$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$ISEXTWIN(5)$` **Returns:** `1`

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: _Maximize text window to full size_

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MTW(window1,window2,...)$`

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text:
```text
$MTW(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
         ───────
         ALL
         CUR
         0-35
         ───────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: This command maximizes a particular text window to full screen using whatever text window font is associated with that text window. This does not affect any text that is already on the screen, only the internal definition of the text window (any scroll margins are reset). The cursor is moved to the home position, but is not re-enabled if it was previously disabled (use [`$CON$`](#con) for this). ANSI color attributes are not changed. The possible settings for the WHICH parameter are:

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | Keyword  | Description                                   |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | `ALL`    | Maximize all text windows at once             |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | `CUR`    | Maximize only the current text window         |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: | `number` | Maximize a particular text window slot number |

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to maximize more than one text window in the same `$MTW$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed.

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: It should be noted that if a text window being maximized is a standard text window created with the [RIP_TEXT_WINDOW](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#rip_text_window) command, or if you just switched to a previously "unused" text window without explicitly defining it with a [RIP_EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW](1.4-terminal-ansi-view.md#rip_extended_text_window) command, then this command will treat the text window still as a "standard" text window. The window is moved to the very upper-left corner of the display. If it was an extended text window, then it is still moved to the upper-left corner of the screen, and the bounding box is made to exactly fit the actual text window display region. Remember, extended text windows don't know anything about text coordinate base locations of the upper-left corner, but standard text windows do. This command maintains this nature of the text window being maximized.

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: If a text window being maximized is currently protected, this command also does nothing to that text window.

requirements.heading: $MTW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MTW(ALL)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: _Restore Text Window information_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$RTW(source)$`

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text:
```text
$RTW(opt:SOURCE)$
         ──────
         BASE
         POP
         0-9
         ──────
     def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified then this command restores all text window definitions from the slot-less definition file saved with a [`$STW$`](#stw) command (with no parameters). The file is not deleted and you can restore many times. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot parameter then that identifies which of the ten different slots you wish to restore from (0-9). Once the slot file is read it is deleted. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot number of "POP" then you are performing a stack-based pop operation (eg, `$RTW(POP)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: If you specify "BASE" instead of a slot number than the text window table will be restored from the text window backup area's base save area. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: In any case, the text window settings active when a `$STW$` (Save Text Window) was executed are saved. The current cursor location, window location, ANSI attributes, cursor ON/OFF status, vertical scrolling margins, and the System Font are restored. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: > **NOTE:** The text contents of the window are not restored.

requirements.heading: $RTW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RTW(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: _Save Text Window information_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$STW(destination)$`

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text:
```text
$STW(opt:DESTINATION)$
         ───────────
         BASE
         PUSH
         0-9
         ───────────
      def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified, then this command stores all currently defined text windows' settings base save area. The windows' X/Y dimensions are preserved, as are the current cursor location, ANSI attributes, cursor ON/OFF status and the vertical scrolling margins. Even the current System Fonts used for all windows are saved (if necessary). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot parameter, then you are specifying to save the text window definitions to one of up to ten different slots (0-9). These allow you to have up to ten different text window configurations saved at the same time. If you save to a slot then when you restore that slot the saved definitions are deleted from the disk. If you don't specify a slot parameter (a slot-less save) then you can restore that definition file multiple times without the file being deleted. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot number of "PUSH" then you are performing a stack-based save operation (eg, `$STW(PUSH)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: If you specify "BASE" instead of a slot number than the text window table will be stored into the text window backup area's base save area. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: > **NOTE:** The contents of the Text Window are not saved.

requirements.heading: $STW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$STW(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: _Return a drawing port’s current graphics-text cursor_

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TEXTXY([port[,domain]])$`

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: Port is CUR or decimal 0..35, default current; domain is WORLD or DEVICE, default WORLD. A domain requires the port argument first: use `$TEXTXY(CUR,DEVICE)$`. Other selectors/domains or more than two arguments reject.

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: WORLD returns the raw stored per-port cursor; DEVICE converts it using the current global world/device dimensions with integer truncation. These domain names do not guarantee the stored units: RIPtel 3.1’s MOVE and outline text paths store converted device positions, while classic TEXT_XY stores a different mixed-unit result. See the [original cursor-update rules](3.0-text-output-and-fonts.md#rip_text_xy). DEVICE can therefore apply another conversion to a pair already converted by its producer. The result is **unpadded signed decimal** `X:Y`, narrowed to signed 16-bit values. Stored (297,321) returns `297:321`; under world/device ratios of 2, DEVICE returns `148:160`.

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: With an explicit port argument, an undefined port or deactivated viewport returns the sentinel `-1`. **Omission differs from explicit CUR:** bare `$TEXTXY$` bypasses that definition/viewport check and reads the current cursor even with a deactivated viewport. It is a current cursor query, not an immutable log of the last rendered string.

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: TEXTXY reads the current cursor after command updates. Nonempty TEXT advances X by its integer string width and retains Y, irrespective of justification/orientation. A later MOVE replaces the query result without text output. Empty TEXT leaves it unchanged silently; empty TEXT_XY leaves it unchanged with an error. Fractional classic CHR raster advances do not produce fractional TEXTXY values: the original metric sums raw glyph widths, scales the entire string and truncates toward zero; two 6.25-pixel advances give integer width 12, while separate one-character TEXT calls each advance 6.

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: **Measured example:** world 1280×960, device 800×600, viewport origin(5,7), classic font 1 with controlled A/B advances 6.25 each. MOVE(10,20) stores(11,19); TEXT("AB") stores(23,19). WORLD/default returns **`23:19`**, DEVICE returns **`14:11`** (another conversion of the stored pair, without removing the origin). Later MOVE(30,40) makes default TEXTXY **`23:32`**. A literal `m(10,20);T("AB")` result therefore depends on active font metrics and conversion/origin state. Under unit mapping/origin 0 it is X=10+integer string width, Y=20. These values come from original cursor/metric instructions and callback checks with controlled glyph drawing; [exact fixture, bytes and derivation](../research/issue-6-macro-evaluation.md#integration-review-exact-textxy-cursor-and-fractional-metrics).

requirements.heading: $TEXTXY$
requirements.text: _Evidence: DLL, callback RVA `0x30ede–0x31051`, cursor fields +0x5c/+0x60 and conversion `0x310b8`; [derivation and original-handler checks](../research/issue-6-macro-evaluation.md)._

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: _Erase text window to line end_

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWERASEEOL(window1,window2`

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWERASEEOL(opt:WINDOW1, ...)$
                ───────
                ALL
                CUR
                0-35
                ───────
            def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: This variable clears the current line in the specified text window from the cursor (inclusive) to the end of the line in the current ANSI color attributes. If the you specify no parameters, then the current text window is used for the destination window. If you do specify any parameters, they must be set to "CUR" for the current text window, "ALL" for all currently defined text windows, or 0-35 to indicate a specific text window slot number.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: You may specify one or more parameters to indicate that you wish to erase more than one text window's current lines in the same `$TWERASEEOL$` statement. If any one of them fails to match the proper parameters, then the entire command is considered a syntax error and none of the parameters are processed.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: If the specified text window is deactivated or undefined then nothing happens for that parameter.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: Unlike many other text window commands, this one can make an actual visual effect on the screen even if the specified text window isn't the current text window.

requirements.heading: $TWERASEEOL$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWERASEEOL(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: _Active Text Font_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWFONT(window)$`

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWFONT(opt:WINDOW)$
            ──────
            CUR
            0-35
            ──────
        def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: This Text Variable returns which of the five Text Window Fonts is active, or 0 (zero) if specified text window is not defined, or is deactivated. The following values are returned: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | Value | Description          |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | 0     | No Text Window       |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | 2     | 91x43 MicroANSI font |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: | 4     | 91x25 MicroANSI font |

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: Note that this command returns the actual text window font number plus one. So to match the returned value to actual RIPscrip text window font numbers, subtract one from this result (providing that it is greater than 0). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a window parameter, then this command refers to the current text window. If you do specify the window number parameter, then you may specify a value of 0-35 for a specific text window data table entry, or the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window (the default). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWFONT(4)$` **Returns:** `1`

requirements.heading: $TWFONT$
requirements.text: The five values match the five terminal text modes listed in RIPtel's MESSAGES.HLP - fonts 2 and 4 are the 91-column [MicroANSI](../techspecs/3.3-microansi-maf-delta.md) modes. _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8734 group)._

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: _Move cursor to X,Y in text window_

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWGOTO(winno,x_pos,y_pos)$`

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWGOTO(req:WINNO, opt:X_POS, opt:Y_POS)$
            ─────      ─────      ─────
            CUR        CUR        CUR
            0-35       0-90       0-42
                       ─────      ─────
                   def=CUR    def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: This variable allows you to move the cursor position in a given text window to a specified X/Y position. If no parameters are given or no X/Y parameters are given then nothing happens when this is executed.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is deactivated, then this command does nothing.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: The WINNO parameter specifies a text window data table entry to move the cursor in. Valid settings for WINNO are 0-35 for a specific text window data table entry, or "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the specified window is not the current text window then the cursor in that window's definition is moved but no visible things occur on the screen. If the specified window is "CUR" or the window number happens to be the current text window, then the cursor that is (potentially) on the screen is moved to the new location.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: The X/Y coordinates are text coordinates (1 based). Specifying both coordinates allows you to place the cursor anywhere in the chosen window. You may omit the Y parameter entirely to move the cursor horizontally only. Either the X or Y parameter (or both) may be specified as "CUR" to indicate the the row or column is not to change. In other words, if you wanted to move the cursor to line 2 in the text window 5, but leave its column unchanged, you would use `$TWGOTO(5,CUR,2)$`.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: If the goto sequence would put the cursor outside the dimensions of the text window then the cursor is placed at the closest point to the given location at the windows border.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: Text locations in this command are zero based (eg, the first column is specified as "0"). If the no X or Y parameters are specified, then this command does nothing because there is no X/Y information to move to.

requirements.heading: $TWGOTO$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWGOTO(CUR,10,2)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: _Text Window Height_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWH(window,type,domain)$`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWH(opt:WINDOW, opt:TYPE, opt:DOMAIN)$
         ──────      ────      ──────
         CUR         BOUND     WORLD
         0-35        CELL      DEVICE
         ──────      TEXT      ROWS:TYPE=TEXT
     def=CUR         ────      ──────
                 def=TEXT  def=ROWS:TYPE=TEXT
                               WORLD:TYPE<>TEXT
```

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If no parameters are specified, then this command returns the height of the current text window in text cells (lines). You may specify a window number to indicate which text window you are inquiring about. The text window number parameters may be a value from 0-35 to reference a specific text window data table entry, or you may specify a keyword of "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is deactivated, then a value of "0" is returned. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If you specify any parameters then they must be in a specific order. The first (already discussed) is the text window number, and if it is omitted, then the current text window is assumed. If you specify two parameters, then you must specify the window number parameter and the type parameter. The type parameter determines what type of information you are inquiring about. If you omit the type parameter then you are inquiring about the text window height itself, in actual text window cell sizes (eg, the window might respond with "5" to indicate that it is 5 lines of text tall. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If you specify the type parameter, then you are directing this command to respond with information about a specific text window piece of information. The available type parameters are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description                                         |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `BOUND` | Return the height of the bounding box in pixels     |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `TEXT`  | Return the height of the display region             |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `CELL`  | Return the height of a text cell in the text window |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The third and final parameter is only of use if the BOUND or CELL parameter is used, and it determines the domain of the pixel size returned by the text variable. The possible values of domain are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `WORLD` | Return the value in world coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `DEVICE` | Return the value in raw device pixel coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: | `ROWS` | Return height of area in text lines (valid only for a type of "TEXT". |

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If the domain parameter is omitted, then it automatically defaults to WORLD (except for the TEXT type, which defaults to the height of the text window in lines of text). When a world coordinate value is returned, the actual "raw" dimensions are converted to the current environment's world coordinate system then returned to the host. If the domain is set to "DEVICE" then the value is returned in raw, device-level pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The BOUND parameter refers to the text window's bounding rectangle. It is the absolute exterior that the text window may extend to. It can also be thought of as a margin outside the actual text window where nothing can be displayed from the text window. See the RIP*EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW for more details about this bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The CELL parameter indicates that you are inquiring about the height of a character cell used in the text window. The height of a cell is based on the font number and resolution currently in use on the actual destination RIPscrip software package. Under 640x350, this was typically 8x8 for font #0 (ie, in RIPscrip 1.54). This may be different now at varying resolutions. So, if you are running at a resolution of 640x350 and you inquire about a text window's cell height for a text window using font #0, then it most likely will return a result of 8 pixels (in device coordinates). The actual value in world coordinates could vary well be different based on the size of the world coordinate resolution frame. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: The "TEXT" type indicates that you are requesting information about the text window sub-section of the text window definition. If the domain parameter is specified, then you are requesting the actual height of the text window display area in "lines of text". This can also be retrieved if the domain parameter is "ROWS". This particular domain parameter known as "ROWS" is only valid for a type parameter of "TEXT". Using it in any other context is considered a syntax error. If the domain parameter is specified, and it is set to "WORLD", then the pixel height of the display region is being requested in world coordinates. If domain is set to DEVICE, then you are requesting the height of the display region in actual hardware pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: It should be noted that the bounding box of a text window can be obtained regardless of whether it is an old-style 1.54 text window created with RIP*TEXT_WINDOW or a new "resolution independent" text window defined via the RIP_EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW command. This can be because under the older text window concept, the bounding box is exactly as large as the text window itself, while under the extended text window, the text window will typically be inside the bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: If you completely omit the type parameter, then you must omit the domain parameter. In this case, you are asking for the height of the text window in "lines of text", not in pixels. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH$` - Height of current text window in lines of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(CUR)$` - Height of current text window in lines of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(5,BOUND)$` - Height of text window 5's bounding box in world coordinates. **Returns:** `800`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(5,BOUND,DEVICE)$` - Height of text window 5's bounding box in device pixel coordinates **Returns:** `400`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(CUR,CELL)` - Height of current text window's character cell in world coordinates. **Returns:** `16`

requirements.heading: $TWH$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWH(5,CELL,DEVICE)$` - Height of text window 5's character cell in device pixel coordinates.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: _Move cursor to home position in text window_

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A1._

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWHOME(winno)$`

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWHOME(opt:WINNO)$
            ─────
            CUR
            0-35
            ─────
        def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: This command moves the cursor in the specified text window data table entry to the upper-left corner of the window. WINNO may be any value from 0-35 to indicate the desired data table entry, or the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the WINNO slot number happens to correspond to the current text window or the WINNO parameter is specified as "CUR" then the cursor that is on the screen (potentially) will be visibly moved. If the WINNO parameter specifies a window that is not the current text window then the cursor position definition for that non-current window is altered only - no visible thing would happen on the screen.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: If the specified window is deactivated or is undefined then nothing happens.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: If the WINNO parameter is omitted then the current text window is assumed.

requirements.heading: $TWHOME$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWHOME(5)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: _Text Window Status_

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWIN(window)$`

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWIN(opt:WINDOW)$
          ──────
          CUR
          0-35
          ──────
      def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: This Text Variable checks to see if the specified Text Window is activated, and returns "YES" if the specified text window is activated or returns "NO" if it is deactivated (eg, with the [`$DTW$`](#dtw) command for example). If the specified text window isn't defined, then this command returns a value of "NO". _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a window parameter, then this command refers to the current text window. If you do specify a window parameter then it can be a value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, or the value "CUR" to indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWIN$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWIN(4)$` **Returns:** `YES`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: _Text Window Width_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWW(window,type,domain)$`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWW(opt:WINDOW, opt:TYPE, opt:DOMAIN)$
         ──────      ────      ──────
         CUR         BOUND     WORLD
         0-35        CELL      DEVICE
         ──────      TEXT      COLS:TYPE=TEXT
     def=CUR         ────      ──────
                 def=TEXT  def=COLS:TYPE=TEXT
                               WORLD:TYPE<>TEXT
```

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If no parameters are specified, then this command returns the width of the current text window in text cells (columns). You may specify a window number to indicate which text window you are inquiring about. The text window number parameters may be a value from 0-35 to reference a specific text window data table entry, or you may specify a keyword of "CUR" to indicate the current text window. If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is deactivated, then a value of "0" is returned. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If you specify any parameters then they must be in a specific order. The first (already discussed) is the text window number, and if it is omitted, then the current text window is assumed. If you specify two parameters, then you must specify the window number parameter and the type parameter. The type parameter determines what type of information you are inquiring about. If you omit the type parameter then you are inquiring about the text window width itself, in actual text window cell sizes (eg, the window might respond with "5" to indicate that it is 5 columns wide. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If you specify the type parameter, then you are directing this command to respond with information about a specific text window piece of information. The available type parameters are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description                                        |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `BOUND` | Return the width of the bounding box in pixels     |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `TEXT`  | Return the width of the display region             |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `CELL`  | Return the width of a text cell in the text window |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: The third and final parameter is only of use if the BOUND or CELL parameter is used, and it determines the domain of the pixel size returned by the text variable. The possible values of domain are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `WORLD` | Return the value in world coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `DEVICE` | Return the value in raw device pixel coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: | `COLS` | Return width of area in text columns (valid only for a type of "TEXT". |

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If the domain parameter is omitted, then it automatically defaults to WORLD (except for the TEXT type, which defaults to the height of the text window in lines of text). When a world coordinate value is returned, the actual "raw" dimensions are converted to the current environment's world coordinate system then returned to the host. If the domain is set to "DEVICE" then the value is returned in raw, device-level pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If the domain parameter is omitted, then it automatically defaults to WORLD (except for the TEXT type, which defaults to the width of the text window in columns of text). When a world coordinate value is returned, the actual "raw" dimensions are converted to the current environment's world coordinate system then returned to the host. If the domain is set to "DEVICE" then the value is returned in raw, device-level pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: The BOUND parameter refers to the text window's bounding rectangle. It is the absolute exterior that the text window may extend to. It can also be thought of as a margin outside the actual text window where nothing can be displayed from the text window. See the RIP*EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW for more details about this bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: The CELL parameter indicates that you are inquiring about the width of a character cell used in the text window. The width of a cell is based on the font number and resolution currently in use on the actual destination RIPscrip software package. Under 640x350, this was typically 8x8 for font #0 (ie, in RIPscrip 1.54). This may be different now at varying resolutions. So, if you are running at a resolution of 640x350 and you inquire about a text window's cell width for a text window using font #0, then it most likely will return a result of 8 pixels (in device coordinates). The actual value in world coordinates could vary well be different based on the size of the world coordinate resolution frame. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: The "TEXT" type indicates that you are requesting information about the text window sub-section of the text window definition. If the domain parameter is specified, then you are requesting the actual width of the text window display area in "columns of text". This can also be retrieved if the domain parameter is "COLS". This particular domain parameter known as "COLS" is only valid for a type parameter of "TEXT". Using it in any other context is considered a syntax error. If the domain parameter is specified, and it is set to "WORLD", then the pixel width of the display region is being requested in world coordinates. If domain is set to DEVICE, then you are requesting the width of the display region in actual hardware pixel coordinates. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: It should be noted that the bounding box of a text window can be obtained regardless of whether it is an old-style 1.54 text window created with RIP*TEXT_WINDOW or a new "resolution independent" text window defined via the RIP_EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW command. This can be because under the older text window concept, the bounding box is exactly as large as the text window itself, while under the extended text window, the text window will typically be inside the bounding rectangle. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: If you completely omit the type parameter, then you must omit the domain parameter. In this case, you are asking for the width of the text window in "text columns", not in pixels. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW$` - Width of current text window in columns of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(CUR)$` - Width of current text window in columns of text. **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(5,BOUND)$` - Width of text window 5's bounding box in world coordinates. **Returns:** `800`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(5,BOUND,DEVICE)$` - Width of text window 5's bounding box in device pixel coordinates **Returns:** `400`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(CUR,CELL)` - Width of current text window's character cell in world coordinates. **Returns:** `16`

requirements.heading: $TWW$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWW(5,CELL,DEVICE)$` - Width of text window 5's character cell in device pixel coordinates.

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: _Text Win Upper Left X Coordinates_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWX0(window,type,domain)$`

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWX0(opt:WINDOW, opt:TYPE, opt:DOMAIN)$
          ──────      ────      ──────
          CUR         BOUND     WORLD
          0-35        TEXT      DEVICE
          ──────      ────      ──────
      def=CUR     def=TEXT  def=WORLD
```

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: This variable returns upper-left X coordinate information about a text window. The exact type and nature of the returned information is determined by the parameters provided (if any). Without any parameters, this command returns the upper-left X coordinate of the text window in text coordinates (see below for a more detailed explanation). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: If the first parameter is provided, then it indicates which text window you requesting information on. It may be set to a numeric value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, or it may be "CUR" to indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: If the specified text window doesn't exist, or is deactivated, then this command returns a value of "-1" to indicate failure. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: > **NOTE:** Under 1.54, this text variable used to return "0" to indicate that a text window was deactivated. This was inaccurately documented in previous RIPscrip releases because "0" could be a valid upper-left X coordinate.

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: If the second parameter, type, is provided, then the window number parameter must be present. The type parameter defines what type of information you are requesting about the text window. The avaiable keyword values for the type parameter are as follows: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description                                              |

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: | `BOUND` | Upper left X coordinate of the bounding rectangle        |

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: | `TEXT`  | Upper left X coordinate of text window display rectangle |

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: The BOUND parameter indicates that you are inquiring about the text window's bounding rectangle's upper left X coordinate. The result is returned in either world coordinates or in physical device coordinates based on the domain parameter (see below). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: The TEXT parameter indicates that you are inquiring about the actual text window's display area somewhere inside the bounding rectangle. The information returned is the upper-left X graphical coordinate of the text window display rectangle. It is returned either in world coordinates or in device pixel coordinates based on the domain parameter (see below). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: The third parameter is only valid if the type parameter is provided. It indicates the domain under which the type parameter data is returned to the host. The possible values for domain are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: | Keyword  | Description                                       |

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: | `WORLD`  | Return information in current world coordinates   |

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: | `DEVICE` | Return information in physical device coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: The domain parameter determines what type of numbers are returned for the bounding box or the text window display rectangle. If this parameter is omitted, then the coordinates are returned in world coordinates. If the parameter is specified, then the result is in either world or device coordinates depending on the value of the parameter. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: If no type parameter is specified (as previously described), then the text window's upper-left X coordinate is returned in text coordinates. This is to maintain backward compability with older RIPscrip v1.54 related commands. In fact, this is not the best way of determining where the text window is on the screen - graphical coordinates are a much better method. If a text window is defined with the RIP*TEXT_WINDOW command where you specify the location of the text window solely on the basis of text coordinate X/Y data, then this form of this command will return a number indicating which X character cell the text window starts at. If the text window is defined using the RIP_EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW command, where the upper-left corner of the text window might not start on an even multiple of the window's cell size, then this command returns a value of "-1" to indicate that the desired request cannot be processed because the text window isn't the right kind of text window. In this manner, the value "-1" is used to indicate that an error has occurred with this command. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX0$` - Upper left X coordinate of the current text window in text coordinates **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX0(CUR)$` - Upper left X coordinate of the current text window in text coordinates **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX0(CUR,BOUND)$` - Upper left X coordinate of the current text window's bounding box in world coordinates. **Returns:** `100`

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX0(CUR,BOUND,WORLD)$` - Upper left X coordinate of the current text window's bounding box in world coordinates. **Returns:** `100`

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX0(CUR,BOUND,DEVICE)$` - Upper left X coordinate of the current text window's bounding box in device pixel coordinates. **Returns:** `50`

requirements.heading: $TWX0$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX0(CUR,TEXT,DEVICE)$` - Upper left X coordinate of the text window's display box in device pixel coordinates. **Returns:** `55`

requirements.heading: $TWX1$

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$TWX1(window,type,domain)$`

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text:
```text
$TWX1(opt:WINDOW, opt:TYPE, opt:DOMAIN)$

The exact type and nature of the returned information is determined by the parameters provided (if any). Without any parameters, this command returns the lower-right X coordinate of the text window in text coordinates (see below for a more detailed explanation). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: If the first parameter is provided, then it indicates which text window you requesting information on. It may be set to a numeric value from 0-35 to indicate a specific text window data table entry, or it may be "CUR" to indicate the current text window. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: If the second parameter, type, is provided, then the window number parameter must be present. The type parameter defines what type of information you are requesting about the text window. The avaiable keyword values for the type parameter are as follows: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: | Keyword | Description                                               |

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: | `BOUND` | Lower right X coordinate of the bounding rectangle        |

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: | `TEXT`  | Lower right X coordinate of text window display rectangle |

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: The BOUND parameter indicates that you are inquiring about the text window's bounding rectangle's lower right X coordinate. The result is returned in either world coordinates or in physical device coordinates based on the domain parameter (see below). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: The TEXT parameter indicates that you are inquiring about the actual text window's display area somewhere inside the bounding rectangle. The information returned is the lower-right X graphical coordinate of the text window display rectangle. It is returned either in world coordinates or in device pixel coordinates based on the domain parameter (see below). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: The third parameter is only valid if the type parameter is provided. It indicates the domain under which the type parameter data is returned to the host. The possible values for domain are: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: | Keyword  | Description                                       |

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: | `WORLD`  | Return information in current world coordinates   |

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: | `DEVICE` | Return information in physical device coordinates |

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: The domain parameter determines what type of numbers are returned for the bounding box or the text window display rectangle. If this parameter is omitted, then the coordinates are returned in world coordinates. If the parameter is specified, then the result is in either world or device coordinates depending on the value of the parameter. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: If no type parameter is specified (as previously described), then the text window's lower-right X coordinate is returned in text coordinates. This is to maintain backward compability with older RIPscrip v1.54 related commands. In fact, this is not the best way of determining where the text window is on the screen - graphical coordinates are a much better method. If a text window is defined with the RIP*TEXT_WINDOW command where you specify the location of the text window solely on the basis of text coordinate X/Y data, then this form of this command will return a number indicating which X character cell the text window starts at. If the text window is defined using the RIP_EXTENDED_TEXT_WINDOW command, where the lower-right corner of the text window might not start on an even multiple of the window's cell size, then this command returns a value of "-1" to indicate that the desired request cannot be processed because the text window isn't the right kind of text window. In this manner, the value "-1" is used to indicate that an error has occurred with this command. *(v2.A4)\_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: When graphical coordinate information is returned on the lower right X location, it is returned based on the resolution independent nature of rectangles in RIPscrip. This means that if the very last most device pixel of text window data is at X coordinate 299, then this command would return a value of 300 for the lower right X coordinate value. See the section on the THE MATHEMATICS OF GRAPHICS AND COORDINATES" for more details about why we use this coordinate convention. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX1$` - Lower right X coordinate of the current text window in text coordinates **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $TWX1$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$TWX1(CUR)$` - Lower right X coordinate of the current text window in text coordinates **Returns:** `5`

requirements.heading: $AVP$
requirements.text: This command does the exact opposite of the [`$DVP$`](#dvp) text variable which deactivates a viewport. When a viewport is activated, it no longer discards graphical commands that are sent to it. This does not make any visual changes on the screen immediately - they only affect subsequent graphical RIPscrip operations that are received when that viewport is selected as the current viewport. You may activate more then one viewport by specifying multiple viewport slot numbers.

requirements.heading: $DVP$
requirements.text: This command deactivates a viewport, making no more RIPscrip graphics commands displayable in that viewport. When a viewport is deactivated, it no longer accepts graphical commands that are sent to it. This does not make any visual changes on the screen immediately; they only affect subsequent graphical RIPscrip operations that are received when that viewport is selected as the current viewport. You may deactivate more then one viewport by specifying multiple viewport slot numbers.

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: _Query offscreen pixel budget or the physical target port_

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$OFFSCREEN([mode])$`

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: At most one case-insensitive mode is accepted:

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: | Mode            | Result                                               |

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: | omitted or FREE | Remaining offscreen pixel budget                     |

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: | USED            | Total minus remaining pixel budget                   |

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: | TOTAL           | Total offscreen pixel budget                         |

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: | CLIP            | Current physical target port number, or -1 when none |

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: Budget results are unsigned decimal pixel counts, independent of Base Math. Port allocation/deletion accounts device width × device height, not bitmap bytes or contents. With total 500000 and free 300000, TOTAL returns `500000`, USED `200000`, FREE `300000`. CLIP is signed decimal and may differ from the current logical port selection. Other modes or extra arguments reject.

requirements.heading: $OFFSCREEN$
requirements.text: The HLP one-liner “offscreen bitmap port pixel data” describes this accounting query; there is **no bitmap-contents readback** in the handler. The inherited screen-size budget example does not establish a universal configured budget for every client instance.

requirements.heading: Port query grammar and RIPtel 3.1 status
requirements.text: Thus the parser accepts `$PORTW$`, `$PORTW(CUR)$`, `$PORTW(CUR,PORT)$`, `$PORTW(CUR,VIEW)$` and `$PORTW(CUR,VIEW,DEVICE)$`; substitute any of the other five names without changing the grammar. A numeric selector remains decimal regardless of Base Math; leading zeroes are accepted. **`(portno,DEVICE)` and `(portno,WORLD)` are not shorthands**: the second field is always a type. Specify `(portno,PORT,DEVICE)` or `(portno,VIEW,DEVICE)` instead. PORTY1 has no separate `(viewno,coordtype)` form. Blank comma fields are discarded by the ordinary variable parser rather than reserving missing positions, so `(CUR,,DEVICE)` cannot skip the type.
requirements.reason: Shared three-field grammar, decimal/leading-zero selectors, every trailing optional prefix and rejection of second-field DOMAIN are independently covered. Ordinary enclosing macro-parser empty-comma collapse is separate pending work; this preexpanded reference boundary rejects empty fields.

requirements.heading: Port query grammar and RIPtel 3.1 status
requirements.text: **Shipped callback defect:** the decoder returns success for these valid forms, but all six RIPtel 3.1 callbacks invert that result, set the variable-error flag and return no value. Ordinary macro expansion leaves each complete expression unchanged; it does not produce the intended numeric width/height/coordinate or sentinel. Invalid forms can fall into calculation with partially uninitialized decoded state, so do not treat an accidental result as an alternate supported grammar or assume a clean rejection. The per-variable dimension descriptions/examples below describe the intended query, not a successful original-client reply. This extends the earlier confirmed PORTW/PORTH defect to the four corner queries; no numerical calculation has been patched to make it pass.

Port number 0 would always yield a value of "0" because its port is set to the full dimensions of the screen so there's no offset information for the upper-left X coordinate.

requirements.heading: $PORTX1$
requirements.text: If no parameters are specified, then you a request is being made for the lower-right X coordinate of the current drawing port itself related to the current screen. This is only meaningful for "screen ports" where this X coordinate specifies an offset from the left border of the screen in pixels. For offscreen bitmapped ports, there is no upper-left X coordinate (or more precisely, an offset from some screen), so for offscreen ports this variation returns a value that is equivalent to the width of the port. Port number 0 would always yield a value that is the width of the actual screen because its port is set to the full dimensions of the screen so there's no offset information for the upper-left X coordinate.

requirements.heading: $APP$
requirements.text: This text variable instructs the terminal to execute an external application. If you do not specify any parameters, then application number zero will be executed. If you do specify any parameters, you may specify one or both of them. If you supply the ARGUMENT parameter, you must specify the APPNO option. APPNO is a number from 0-9 indicating which application should be executed. If used, the ARGUMENT parameter is an arbitrary command line argument that will be added to the end of the application's command line string. This gives the ability to allow the host to control portions of the external application's operation.

requirements.reason: Reference adoption reopens this claim: the containing document changed in PR #71. Existing implementation/tests are historical evidence, pending reconciliation with the new contract. Previous review: Ordinary D requires one decimal duration 1..65535, emits no replacement text and starts the input gate using the detailed 60ths rule. Tests cover boundaries, failures preserving gates, nonfatal recovery and owned immediate-query continuation across multiple/final delays before later input. The milliseconds summary remains separately blocked under #46; full interaction/application gating remains pending.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: **Syntax:** `$D(required:duration)$`; documented ordinary range **1..65535**, in **60ths of a second**, not milliseconds.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: RIPtel 3.1 converts the duration to an integer-millisecond clock interval, truncating the fraction: **`floor(duration × 1000 / 60)`** for ordinary values. Its original helper divides long waits into 3900-tick (65000 ms) chunks plus the final floored remainder; these chunks preserve the same total conversion.

requirements.text: | Expression  | Converted clock interval           |

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: | `$D(1)$`    | **16 ms**, from truncating 1000/60 |

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: These are timer targets, not exact wall-clock durations; clock granularity, phase and scheduling affect elapsed time. The summary's inherited "milliseconds" wording was incorrect. The detailed tick rule and [inventory](9.1-text-variable-reference.md#terminal-operation) units were correct.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: The variable performs a **synchronous busy wait** on the evaluating thread, polling `timeGetTime` until each deadline. It does not return immediately after installing a nonblocking input gate, pump input in that loop or dispatch the separate [wire RIP_DELAY](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_delay) handler. Ordinary macro expansion continues on the same call stack after the wait and emits no replacement text.

requirements.heading: $D$
requirements.text: **Shipped validation quirks:** exactly one argument is required, but the original callback checks only that its first character is a digit before decimal prefix conversion. It has no explicit 1..65535 gate: `$D(0)$` and `$D(65536)$` are accepted; `$D(1A)$` and `$D(1.5)$` behave as `$D(1)$`. A leading sign, space, letter or empty value rejects the variable. These observations do not extend the documented portable range to arbitrary oversized numeric conversions. The helper also compares unsigned absolute timer deadlines without rollover correction; a deadline that wraps can finish early. _Evidence: original registered callback/helper and exhaustive 0..65536/boundary/prefix/fake-clock tests; [derivation](../research/issue-46-delay-variable-units.md)._

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: Deletes the **first existing match for each supplied filename**, using ordinary resource resolution: **configured host directory → shared ICONS directory → user icon-search-path entries in order**. Without a configured host directory, start with shared ICONS, then the search path. Only that first match is passed to deletion; a failed deletion does not fall through to another directory. A missing filename is ignored. Case and the supplied extension are retained; no default extension or legacy ICN/HIC/MSK renaming is performed here.

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: At least one parsed argument is required. Each argument is processed independently, and failure for one does not stop later arguments. This active variable returns no text and supplies no per-file success result; failed lookups/deletions do not set a variable error. Zero arguments set the variable syntax-error flag. Generic parsing limits each argument to 20 characters and omits empty comma fields; `FILEDEL()` therefore has no arguments.

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: **The host-created restriction is a caller precondition.** The inherited specification requires the host to name only files it created or downloaded. RIPtel 3.1's original deletion path has **no ownership ledger, creator/session check or host identity check**: a preexisting shared/search-path file can be its first match. Changing connections or sessions does not create such a check. User search paths are consequently eligible for FILEDEL deletion even though asset delivery does not write new files there.

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: **Path syntax in the original macro expression:** hosts should supply bare filenames. The inherited “path information will be ignored” statement is not a uniform basename rule. The ordinary dollar-argument parser rejects `/`, wildcards and several punctuation characters; a single backslash acts as an escape and disappears before lookup. The examples below are literal macro-expression characters supplied to the expander, after any surrounding transport/command decoding:

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | Parameter text | Original processing |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `DIR\X.BMP` | Resolves filename `DIRX.BMP`, with no directory component |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `..\X.BMP` | Resolves filename `..X.BMP`, with no parent-directory separator |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `\X.BMP` | Resolves filename `X.BMP` |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `C:\DIR\X.BMP` | Resolves `C:DIRX.BMP` beneath each directory prefix; it keeps the configured directory prefix |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `C:X.BMP` | Colon is retained; the OS decides whether the prefixed path is valid |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `DIR/X.BMP`, `../X.BMP`, `/X.BMP` | Expression rejected, no lookup/deletion |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | UNC-style consecutive backslashes, trailing backslash | Expression rejected, no lookup/deletion |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `*.BMP`, `X?.BMP`, `[X].BMP` | Expression rejected, no wildcard expansion or lookup |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: | `.`, `..`, leading/interior spaces | Passed as literal names; this is not a guarantee that the OS can delete them |

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: Rejected argument syntax leaves the expression literal rather than executing FILEDEL. A later ordinary backslash-processing step can alter that literal text without executing the command in the same pass. Direct calls to the lower deletion helper have different tail-stripping behavior; those observations are not a promise that the wire parser accepts the same inputs. See the [complete parser/helper matrix](../research/issue-20-filedel-scope.md#parser-and-helper-are-different-layers).

requirements.heading: $FILEDEL$
requirements.text: _Evidence: original DLL registration 0x26587, callback 0x28434, deletion helper 0x4524c, full resource lookup 0x3f80e, argument parser 0x15602 / 0x155bf and unlink 0x6b480; [derivation and native first-hit/path checks](../research/issue-20-filedel-scope.md). The earlier host-directory-only deletion note was an unverified hypothesis and is superseded by this executable evidence._

requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text:
```text
$OPTION(req:OPTION_NAME, opt:MODE)$
            ───────────      ────
            LIST             ON:OPTION_NAME<>LIST
            DOORWAY          OFF:OPTION_NAME<>LIST
            HOTKEY           QUERY:OPTION_NAME<>LIST
            STATBAR          ────
            TAB          def=<none>:OPTION_NAME=LIST
                             QUERY:OPTION_NAME<>LIST
```

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: This command allows you to turn on or turn off a specific system option in the RIPscrip application. The possible options that can be enabled or disabled are specified with the \<name\> parameter as follows: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: | Name    | Description                                                   |

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: | HOTKEY  | Alter the status of Hotkey processing                         |

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: | TAB     | Alter the status of Tab mouse-field navigation                |

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: | DOORWAY | Alter the status of Doorway (tm) mode                         |

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: | STATBAR | Alter the status of the terminal program's status bar         |

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: | LIST    | Display a list of all options that can be toggled (see below) |

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: After the \<name\> parameter comes the \<mode\> parameter which specifies whether to turn the option on or off. The possible values for the \<mode\> parameter are "ON" and "OFF". _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: The LIST keyword is designed to list out all options in the software that can be enabled or disabled. This allows for extendibility for custom RIPscrip packages by other vendors - some vendors may have certain features, and others may not. For example, if a specific terminal program doesn't support Doorway Mode, then the DOORWAY option wouldn't be available (and wouldn't show up if you did a `$OPTION(LIST)$` directive). The list is not carriage return delimited. The text returned to the host is not terminated with any carriage returns or anything like that. It's up to you to provide that kind of information in a button's host string or in a query string. The LIST directive though returns a list of all recognized keywords for that terminal. For example, RIPterm Pro returns the following for the `$OPTION(LIST)$` expression: _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text:
```text
DOORWAY,HOTKEY,LIST,STATBAR,TAB
```

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: Note, the list is comma (,) delimited between keywords, but not after the last keyword. In addition, the keywords are returned in alphabetical order, converted to all capitals. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $OPTION$
requirements.text: You may ask the terminal to report the status of a particular option with this command as well. To do so, specify a \<mode\> of "QUERY" or omit it altogether. If the option is enabled, a "1" is returned to the host. If it is disabled, then "0" is returned. Again, no carriage returns or other delimiters are returned to the host.

requirements.text:
**Example:** `$OPTION(DOORWAY, ON)$`  
**Returns:** nothing - enabled doorway mode

requirements.heading: $OPTION$

**Returns:** `DOORWAY,HOTKEY,LIST,STATBAR,TAB`

requirements.heading: $OPTION$

**Returns:** `0`

requirements.text: _Query the current Shift-key state_

requirements.heading: $SHIFT$

requirements.heading: $SHIFT$

requirements.heading: $HOSTDIR$
requirements.text: _Query or select the host resource directory_

requirements.heading: $HOSTDIR$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$HOSTDIR([name])$`

requirements.heading: $HOSTDIR$
requirements.text: With no argument, including `$HOSTDIR()$`, return the selected directory name uppercased, or `<NONE>` when none is selected. The getter uppercases the stored name in place. With one argument, trim whitespace and uppercase it. Exact **OFF** clears the selection without attempting creation. Otherwise require at most 12 bytes, reject exact `.` and `..`, and reject any of `\ : * ? + / " , ; > < = [ ] |`. Interior spaces are accepted. Store the name and attempt to create `installation-root\name`; creation failure does not roll back selection. Successful setters return no text. Extra arguments or invalid names reject.

requirements.heading: $HOSTDIR$
requirements.text: A whitespace-only argument becomes empty and clears selection while attempting root-path creation. Empty parentheses are the getter, and `HOSTDIR("")` is a parser error. This variable has no explicit host-service-callback gate. Its clear keyword is **OFF**, whereas [`RIP_SWITCH_DIRECTORY`](6.2-asset-delivery-and-storage.md#rip_switch_directory) recognizes literal `$OFF$` before its own expansion stage. Parameter text in the variable is not a recursively evaluated expression; preprocessing can compose it before the dollar parser runs.

requirements.heading: $HOSTDIR$
requirements.text: _Evidence: DLL, callback RVA `0x28635–0x28812`, original setter `0x6b36` and creation helper `0x3f5ff`; [derivation and state/path probes](../research/issue-6-macro-evaluation.md)._

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: _Request a block-mode file transfer_

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$XFER(direction,protocol,type[,filename…])$` **Returns:** nothing.

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: The first three arguments are required. Keywords are case-insensitive; direction SEND maps to upload mode 1, RECEIVE to download mode 0. Protocol keywords map to the [`RIP_ENTER_BLOCK_MODE`](5.5-file-transfer-and-queries.md#rip_enter_block_mode) protocol codes:

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | Code | Keyword   |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 0    | XMODEM    |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 1    | XMODEMCRC |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 2    | XMODEM1K  |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 3    | XMODEM1KG |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 4    | KERMIT    |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 5    | YMODEM    |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 6    | YMODEMG   |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 7    | ZMODEM    |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | 8    | ZMODEMCR  |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | Type keyword | Block-mode file-type code |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | RIP          | 0                         |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | NONE         | 1                         |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | IMAGE        | 3                         |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: | ACTIVE       | 5                         |

requirements.heading: $XFER$
requirements.text: SEND always requires at least one filename. The shared parser limits each filename argument to 20 bytes and the whole list to 40 arguments (at most 37 filename arguments after the three keywords). RECEIVE protocols 0..4 also require one; RECEIVE protocols 5..8 do not require filenames and ignore any supplied filename arguments. Required filenames are joined with spaces and the `<>` block-mode terminator is appended. The handler invokes RIP_ENTER_BLOCK_MODE with decoded fields `(direction,protocol,type,0)` and that filename tail; this is the same transfer path and capability/refusal behavior, not a separate engine promising support for every keyword. Invalid keywords or missing required arguments reject. Empty comma fields do not supply a missing filename.

requirements.text: These text variables reset particular aspects of the RIPscrip environment. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: RIPscrip Reset Related Text Variables
requirements.text: Bare `$RESET$` is inherited from 1.54: it performs the same operation as [RIP_RESET_WINDOWS](1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_reset_windows) (a "soft" reset); SyncTERM implements it as its full-reset handler. 3.x keeps parameterized reset dispatch. The table below summarizes selected recovered operations; it is not a complete keyword/argument grammar inferred from help strings. The inherited draft entry below remains a separate account of the older general reset design. In particular, TV and TW are distinct callbacks, and [TV requires a variable name](#resettvname).

requirements.heading: $RESET(TV,name)$
requirements.text: _Delete one named user text variable_

requirements.heading: $RESET(TV,name)$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$RESET(TV,name)$` **Returns:** nothing.

requirements.heading: $RESET(TV,name)$
requirements.text: Exactly two nonempty arguments are required after empty comma fields are omitted. The variable name must be shorter than 20 bytes, start with an alphabetic byte, and continue with alphanumeric bytes or underscores. Lookup checks memory first, then the persistent store. If absent, nothing happens. If present and unprotected, delete the matching record. A protected record prompts for confirmation: No retains it, Yes deletes it. The original dialog branch cancels specifically on the No response; no other response is separately rejected. Deletion does not reset text windows or all variables.

requirements.heading: $RESET(TV,name)$
requirements.text: `$RESET(TV)$` and `$RESET(TV,)$` reject for missing name. The separate TW keyword is a text-window reset operation; TV is not its renamed alias. Successful deletion and absent-record no-op return no replacement text; invalid arity/name marks a syntax error. The generic name validator’s empty-string edge cannot turn a missing field into “delete all,” because that field is omitted by the parser.

requirements.heading: $RESET(TV,name)$
