requirements.text: **Format:** `$RESET(option,element,sub_element)$`

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text:
```text
$RESET(opt:OPTION, opt:ELEMENT, opt:SUB_ELEMENT)$
           ──────      ───────
           SOFT        CUR:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,ENV,
                                  VIEW
           HARD        0-35:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,
                                   ENV,VIEW
           MCURSOR     TBL:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,ENV,
                                  MOUSE,VIEW
           KEYBOARD    BASE:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,
                                   ENV,MOUSE,SCREEN
           SOUND       S0-S9:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,
                                    ENV,MOUSE,SCREEN
           TW          SLOTS:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,
                                    ENV,MOUSE,SCREEN
           STYLE       STACK:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,
                                    ENV,MOUSE,SCREEN
           BUT         BACKUP:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,
                                     ENV,MOUSE,SCREEN
           PAL         ALL:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,
                                  ENV,MOUSE,SCREEN,QUERY
           PORT        TW:OPTION=QUERY
           ENV                   VIEW:OPTION=QUERY
           MOUSE       ───────
           SCREEN  def=ALL:OPTION=QUERY
           VIEW        <none>:OPTION=HARD,MCURSOR,KEYBOARD,
           QUERY                     SOUND,SCREEN
           ──────      CUR:OPTION=TW,STYLE,BUT,PAL,PORT,ENV,
       def=SOFT                   VIEW
                       TBL:OPTION=MOUSE

       opt:SUB_ELEMENT
           ───────────
           ALL:ELEMENT=TW,VIEW
           CUR:ELEMENT=TW,VIEW
           TBL:ELEMENT=TW,TBL
           ───────────
       def=ALL:OPTION=QUERY
           <none>:OPTION<>QUERY
```

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: The reset text variable is a general purpose reset command. Without any parameters, the text variable adheres to the original 1.54 RIPscrip command which performs the exact same operations as a [RIP_RESET_WINDOWS](1.3-world-view-virtual-canvas.md#rip_reset_windows) command. Some parameters used with the reset command require additional parameters to further specify what section is to be reset (eg, if you specify "TW" to reset a text window, you need to specify what text window [data table](7.1-data-tables.md) entry is to be reset). The possible reset "types" are as follows:

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | Reset type | Uses Parms | Description                                    |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | SOFT       | No         | Performs a soft reset (like RIP_RESET_WINDOWS) |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | HARD       | No         | Performs a hard reset (like RIP_HEADER)        |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | MCURSOR    | No         | Reset mouse cursor to standard cursor shape    |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | KEYBOARD   | No         | Reset keyboard state back to input status      |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | SOUND      | No         | Stops any currently playing digitized sound    |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | TW         | Yes        | Reset aspects of the text window system        |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | STYLE      | Yes        | Reset aspects of the graphical style system    |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | BUT        | Yes        | Reset aspects of the button style system       |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | PAL        | Yes        | Reset aspects of the color palette system      |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | PORT       | Yes        | Reset aspects of the drawing port system       |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | ENV        | Yes        | Reset aspects of the environment system        |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | MOUSE      | Yes        | Resets the mouse table (clears all entries)    |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | SCREEN     | Yes        | Resets aspects of the screen system            |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | VIEW       | Yes        | Resets aspects drawing port viewports          |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | QUERY      | Yes        | Resets resident queries (clears them)          |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: The following paragraphs describe the purpose of each parameter and how each parameter operations:

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **SOFT** - This makes the reset command perform a soft reset. This is identical in nature to the `RIP_RESET_WINDOWS` command. See that RIPscrip command for a complete, detailed description of what a soft reset does.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **HARD** - This performs a hard reset command. This is as if you issued the `RIP_HEADER` command with the "hard reset" flag enabled. See the `RIP_HEADER` command for more details about a hard reset.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **MCURSOR** - When this parameter is specified then the mouse cursor on the terminal is switched to its default, arrow shape. If the mouse input is currently disabled (via a `RIP_HEADER` command), then it is once again re-enabled as if a `RIP_NO_MORE` command were received.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **KEYBOARD** - When this parameter is specified, then keyboard input is once again enabled. Keyboard input can only be disabled via the `RIP_HEADER` command, and typically is re-enabled by a `RIP_NO_MORE` sequence. This allows you to explicitly re-enable the keyboard without a `RIP_NO_MORE` command being specified.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **SOUND** - This reset command stops any playing digitized sound (if any). If the sound is currently in the process of playing, it is aborted immediately to where there's no sound playing anymore.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **TW** - This parameter allows you to reset certain aspects of the text the text window system. The exact operation depends on what text window is being acted upon. If text window #0 is being reset, then it is set to full screen (no window clearing is performed). If it refers to a text window other than text window #0, then that window is formally deleted. If the current text window is a window other than window #0 and it is reset, then the text window is automatically switched to text window #0. If the reset affects a [data backup area](7.2-data-backup-areas.md), then the data backup area in question is deleted entirely. If you specify no parameters, then the current text window is reset. You may specify one or more parameters with this command to specifically alter particular aspects of the text window system. You may specify the following parameters:

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | Parameter | Description                                                     |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | CUR       | Reset the current text window.                                  |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | 0-35      | Reset a specific text window data table entry.                  |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | TBL       | Reset all text window data table entries.                       |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | BASE      | Reset (clear) the text window base save area                    |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | S0-S9     | Reset (clear) a specific text window data save slot             |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | SLOTS     | Reset (clears) all text window data save slots                  |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | STACK     | Reset (clears) the text window data save stack.                 |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | BACKUP    | Reset all text window backup areas (base area, slots and stack. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | ALL       | Reset all text window data tables and backup areas              |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RESET(TW, CUR, 30, BASE, S5)$`

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **STYLE** - This parameter resets a graphical style back to its default settings. If you specify no parameters, then the current graphical style is reset to bootup defaults. You may specify one or more parameters with this command to specifically alter particular aspects of the graphics style system. You may specify the following parameters:

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.text: | BASE | Reset (clear) the graphical style base save area |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | SLOTS | Reset (clears) all graphical style data save slots. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | STACK | Clears the graphical style data save stack. |

requirements.text: | BACKUP | Reset (clears) all graphical style backup areas (base area, slots and stack. |

If you specify no parameters, then the current button style is reset to bootup defaults. You may specify one or more parameters with this command to specifically alter particular aspects of the button style system. You may specify the following parameters:

Specific-slot and table reset use the ordinary default record. See the [complete button defaults and reset contract](4.3-buttons.md#initial-and-reset-style) and [native derivation](../research/issue-27-button-style-contract.md).

requirements.text: **Example:** `$RESET(PAL, CUR, 30, BASE, S5)$`

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **Shipped palette lifecycle:** resetting an unprotected nonzero slot restores default RGB values and **clears its defined/in-use flag**. Resetting an already undefined unprotected slot leaves it undefined; it does not error or define it. A protected specific/current slot rejects unchanged; TBL and SOFT skip protected slots. HARD removes their protection and resets all nonzero slots to undefined. Slot zero remains defined and unprotectable. Reset preserves the current palette index, except HARD selects zero, so a selected palette can become undefined after a specific/TBL/SOFT reset. Reselecting it with `$CUR(PAL,n)$` defines it again. See the [palette lifecycle truth table](7.1-data-tables.md#palette-reset-lifecycle) and [original reset/status probes](../research/issue-16-table-lifecycle.md).

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: After selecting/modifying palette 5, `$RESET(PAL,5)$` yields `$INUSE(PAL,5)$` = `0`, `$ISPROT(PAL,5)$` = `-1`, and `$CUR(PAL)$` = `5`. Numeric ISPROT checks definition first; its separate CUR form directly tests current protection and returns `0` for this undefined-but-current unprotected slot.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **PORT** - This variation on the reset command resets one or more ports in some way. The exact way that one is reset varies depending on the type of port specified. If no additional parameters are specified, then the current port is reset. Otherwise, you may reset a specific port number in the port data table, or one (or all) of the port data backup areas. If you reset a specific port in the port data table, what happens varies depending on what kind of port it is. If it is port #0 (which cannot be deleted), then the only thing that happens is that any resident queries for that port/viewport are deleted, the viewport is made full screen and the viewport is erased to the background color (in that order). If the port number (from 1-35) represents a screen port, then any resident query attached to that port/viewport is deleted and the port itself is deleted. If it is an offscreen port, then that port is also deleted (offscreen ports cannot have resident queries). In any event, if the port being deleted happens to be the current port, then the port is automatically switched to port #0 (the screen's port). The following parameters are permitted with this reset port). Whenever the current port is reset, the port is automatically switched to port #0. Beware of this when chaining multiple port resets together at the same time. For example, if port #5 is current and you issue the following command `$RESET(PORT, 5, CUR)$`, then port number 5 will be deleted, then it would switch back to port #0 which is the screen port and cannot be deleted, so only its viewport will be reset. The following parameters are permitted with this reset command to control what type of reset operation is to be performed:

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | Parameter | Description |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | CUR | Reset (delete) the current port. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | 0-35 | Reset (delete) a specific port data table entry. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | TBL | Reset (delete) all port data table entries. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | BASE | Reset (clear) the port base save area. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | S0-S9 | Reset (clear) a specific port data save slot. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | SLOTS | Reset (clears) all port data save slots. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | STACK | Reset (clears) the port data save stack. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | BACKUP | Reset (clears) all port backup areas (base area, slots and stack. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | ALL | Reset all port data tables and backup areas |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RESET(PORT, CUR, 30, BASE, S5)$`

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **MOUSE** - Resets (deletes) all mouse fields defined in the specified specified destination. If no parameter is defined, then all current mouse definitions are reset. If you specify one or more parameters, then they may be any of the following:

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.text: **SCREEN** - When no parameters are specified, the entire video screen is cleared to color #0 (usually black). No viewports are modified, nor are any drawing ports, text windows, mouse fields or anything else. The following parameters are allowed, providing you with the ability to reset particular screen aspects:

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | Parameter | Description                                               |

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **VIEW** - When no parameters are specified, then the viewport of the current drawing port is reset to the full dimensions of the port itself, and activated. Other possible parameters allow you to modify other viewports of other ports. The possible parameters are:

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **QUERY** - If no parameters are specified or a single parameter of "ALL" is specified then all resident queries are reset (deleted). If you specify any parameters, you may specify more than one. You may specify the following as the first parameters:

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | TW        | Reset the text window based resident queries |

requirements.heading: $RESET$

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: The next parameter(s) (if any) indicate the data table entry number that you wish to reset. If no parameters are specified, then all queries for the given data type (text window or viewport) will be reset. If you specify an actual data table entry number, then you are deleting the query for a specific text window or viewport (a fixed resident query). You are allowed to use the following parameters after the TW or VIEW directives:

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | Parameter | Description |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | ALL | Reset the current window query and all fixed queries |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | CUR | Reset the "current window" query for the given reset type (ie, TW or VIEW) |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | TBL | Reset all entry-specific queries (ie, reset all resident queries for all specific text windows or viewports. The "current window" query isn't reset. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: | 0-35 | Reset the resident query for the specified data table entry for the given TW or VIEW query type. |

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: See the `RIP_QUERY` command for more detailed information about the various possible resident query types.

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: **Example:**

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text:
```text
$RESET(QUERY, TW, CUR)$ ... Reset current text window's query
$RESET(QUERY, TW, TBL)$ ... Reset all queries for entries 0-35
$RESET(QUERY, TW, 5)$ ..... Reset resident query for Text window #5
```

requirements.heading: $RESET$
requirements.text: It should be noted that if you attempt to reset something that cannot be reset (eg, drawing port #0, a protected data table entry, a stack that's empty, etc), then this command does nothing and does not generate a syntax error. A syntax error can only be generated if an invalid parameter is encountered. If even so much as a single parameter is invalid then the entire command is discarded as a syntax error without any of the parameters being processed.

requirements.heading: $COLORMODE$
requirements.text: If this variable has no parameters, then it queries the [color mode](2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md) of the current environment. It responds with a number that indicates whether or not the terminal is in direct RGB encoding mode or if it is in color palette mapping mode. If the value is 0, then it is palette mapping mode. If it a value from 1-8, then it is in direct RGB encoding mode and the value indicates how many bits of precision are used for the red, green and blue color components separately in RGB encoded data (a value of 8 indicates that 3x8 bits are used, or that we will be working with 24-bit color numbers). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $COLORMODE$
requirements.text: **Shipped wire/macro distinction:** this variable accepts RGB precisions **1..8**, stores them in the selected defined environment, and applies them through the shared active setter when that environment is current. Queries can return **1..7**, in addition to 0 and 8. The eight-bit-only restriction belongs to the **wire [RIP_SET_COLOR_MODE](2.0-color-modes-and-palettes.md#rip_set_color_mode)** handler; it must not be copied into this variable’s table. These are verified state/query results, not a claim about exact color conversion at every precision. _Evidence: original callbacks/active setter, original wire handler and [native range and macro-expansion matrix](../research/issue-23-environment-query-names.md#native-callback-activation-and-wire-checkpoint)._

requirements.heading: $COLORMODE$
requirements.text: **Ownership/protection (RIPtel 3.1):** the callback requires an already defined target, changes only its environment record, and activates the new precision only when that target is current. It bypasses environment protection. The wire color-mode command instead checks environment protection. Current style protection has no effect, and no style record contains a second color-mode copy. See [environment switching and its departing-record overwrite defect](7.1-data-tables.md#environment-table). _Evidence: [original callback/selector and native cases](../research/issue-24-drawing-state-ownership.md#ownership-and-switching-observations)._

requirements.heading: $RESTOREALL$
requirements.text: This performs the eight independent backup-family operations below in the original driver's order. The screen step contains no graphics/button styles or viewport snapshot of its own; those come from their separate table operations. Status-bar visibility is not part of any family. See the [complete capture, palette-binding and failure/lifetime contract](7.2-data-backup-areas.md#screen-save-area). _Evidence: [original wrappers, serializers and native checks](../research/issue-26-screen-backups.md)._

requirements.heading: $RESTOREALL$
requirements.text:
- [`$RTW(slot)$`](#rtw)
- [`$RCB(slot)$`](#rcb)
- [`$RMF(slot)$`](#rmf)
- [`$RESTORE(slot)$`](#restore)
- [`$RCP(slot)$`](#rcp)
- [`$RBS(slot)$`](#rbs)
- [`$RGS(slot)$`](#rgs)
- [`$RENV(slot)$`](#renv)

requirements.heading: $RESTOREALL$
requirements.text: For a numbered slot, all eight restore attempts run first, then all eight delete attempts in the same order. A failed restore can therefore still consume an unprotected saved slot; protected snapshots survive deletion. Base restores do not consume. POP operates independently on each family's stack. Failures do not stop later families and there is no rollback. The existing PORT cursor and STYLE selection restore defects also apply.

requirements.heading: $RESTOREALL$
requirements.text: This command does not require any parameters. If none are specified then the restore is slot-less and can be restored many times. The ability to specify a slot gives you the ability to have restore one of many screen configurations. You are allowed up to ten separate slots (0-9). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RESTOREALL$
requirements.text: In place of a slot number, you can provide a parameter of "POP" to perform a stack-based pop operation to restore the last pushed SAVEALL (eg, `$RESTOREALL(POP)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RESTOREALL$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RESTOREALL(0)$` **Returns:** nothing

The second parameter is the width of the world coordinate frame and the third and final parameter is the height of the coordinate frame. requirements.heading: $WORLD$
requirements.text: **Shipped validation defect:** WORLD rejects an explicit pair only if **both** integers exceed 65535. If just one does, it stores each low 16 bits: `$WORLD(CUR,65536,1)$` sets and queries as **`0:1`**. By contrast, the wire command rejects if **either** dimension exceeds 65535. Both paths accept 32768..65535; the white paper’s advertised 32767 limit is not a setter gate. This describes stored/active world state, not uniform signedness or defined behavior of every later drawing operation on a zero-size frame. _Evidence: [original handlers and boundary matrices](../research/issue-23-environment-query-names.md#native-callback-activation-and-wire-checkpoint)._

requirements.heading: $WORLDH$
requirements.text: This function is used to either set or query the setting of the world coordinate system in the Y direction. If no parameters are specified (eg, `$WORLDH$`) or a single "CUR" parameter is specified, then the current environment's world coordinate Y dimension is returned to the host. If you would like to inquire about a specific environment's world Y setting, specify the environment table entry number as the only parameters (eg, `$WORLDH(5)$` inquires about environment #5's world coordinate Y setting). _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $WORLDH$
requirements.text: The intended two-argument form names an environment and a decimal height, but the shipped setter has the target-selection defect below. Values **0..65535** are accepted; values above 65535 reject.

requirements.heading: $WORLDH$
requirements.text: **Shipped setter defect:** with two arguments, a case-insensitive **CUR first argument causes variable error and leaves state unchanged**. Any other first argument instead modifies the **current** environment, ignoring the target text; this includes a numeric noncurrent/undefined slot and even an invalid name. The query forms still honor numeric targets and return **`-1`** for undefined slots without variable error. Use the complete [WORLD](#world) setter to address a specific environment reliably. _Evidence: original WORLDH/WORLDW callbacks and [native current/target/range matrix](../research/issue-23-environment-query-names.md#native-callback-activation-and-wire-checkpoint)._

requirements.heading: Clipboard Related Text Variables
requirements.text: These text variables return information on, or manipulate the clipboard aspects of the port system. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: Clipboard Related Text Variables
requirements.text: _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:8483/8530 save-restore groups; 9048 `rv_paste`)._

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: _Paste Clipboard at last location_

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: _Added in RIPscrip v2.A4._

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$PCB(portno)$`

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text:
```text
$PCB(opt:PORTNO)$
         ──────
         CUR
         0-35
         ──────
     def=CUR
```

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: This text variable copies a portion of the specified port onto the current drawing port (these ports may be the same). The area on the specified port that is considered to be the source is "remembered" from the last rectangle of data that was put on this port. What this means is when you perform a `RIP_PORT_COPY` command, you copy a rectangle of data from one port to another. The two rectangles of information are stored in the destination port of the copy operation. If the original port were port 0 and the destination port were port 5, then both rectangles of data are stored in port 5's definition. If you switch to port #0 and then perform a `$PCB(5)$` operation, then the rectangle of data on port #5 is copied back to its original location in the current port.

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: This variable is extremely useful for restoring graphics that were previously saved to an offscreen port. It is typically used in dialog boxes when the user clicks on the "OK" button, where the dialog box should be erased and the original graphical screen would be restored.

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: If no parameters are specified, then the port that will be pasted from will be whatever port is associated with the clipboard pointer. See the `RIP_GET_IMAGE` command for more details on the clipboard pointer.

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: If you do specify a parameter, then it can be "CUR" to indicate the current port, or a value 0-35 to specify a specific port number to retrieve the data from. Note that if the specified port doesn't exist, or if either the current port or the specified port are "deactivated", then this command is ignored.

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: It should be noted that the rectangles of information stored in the specified port are "viewport relative". What this means is that the coordinates in those rectangles are based on viewports. If you copy data from say port 0 to port 5, then change port 0's viewport before you perform a `$PCB(5)$` operation, then when you actually perform the `$PCB(5)$` command, the data will be pasted in a new location on the screen - not where it came from. If you're going to be using this command, be careful how you manipulate your viewports.

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$PCB(5)$` ... Paste port 5's data to the current port **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $PCB$
requirements.text: This is the standard "dismiss dialog, restore what was underneath" idiom; the demo entry/exit scripts comment it "Paste original screen image back". The executable paste name is **PCB**. RIPTEL.HLP’s `$P$` shorthand is not registered by the driver or client; [P follows the user-variable path](#p). _Evidence: 2.00a4; HLP; SyncTERM (ripper.c:9048 `rv_paste`); corpus (MENU.ENT, TEL3X2.ENT)._

requirements.heading: $P$
requirements.text: _Not a predefined paste alias in the shipped contract_

requirements.heading: $P$
requirements.text: The 179 built-in driver registrations contain PCB and no P; the client’s additional registrations also contain no P. Actual parsing/evaluation of `$P$` falls through to user-variable lookup, so it may refer to an ordinary user variable named P and is not a paste operation. Use [`$PCB$`](#pcb) for clipboard/port paste. The help-table shorthand is explicitly excluded as a predefined alias, rather than supplied with guessed syntax.

requirements.heading: $P$
requirements.text: _Evidence: DLL registration/lookup and static RIPtel client registration audit; [derivation](../research/issue-6-macro-evaluation.md)._

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: _Restore Clipboard_

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$RCB$(source)`

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text:
```text
$RCB(opt:SOURCE)$
         ──────
         BASE
         POP
         0-9
         ──────
     def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: This Active Text Variable restores the Clipboard from a previously executed [`$SCB$`](#scb) command. Not only are the clipboard contents saved, but so is the last clipboard location, so Paste Clipboard ([`$PCB$`](#pcb)) restores the clipboard's contents AND location.

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a slot parameter then the clipboard is restored from a slot-less file. It is not deleted so you can do multiple identical clipboard restorations. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: If you do specify a slot parameter then you may restore the clipboard from any of ten different clipboard slots (0-9). Once restored, the clipboard slot file is deleted. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: You may specify a slot number of "POP" to perform a stack-based pop operation (eg, `$RCB(POP)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RCB$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RCB(4)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: _Save Clipboard_

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$SCB(destination)$`

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text:
```text
$SCB(opt:DESTINATION)$
         ───────────
         BASE
         PUSH
         0-9
         ───────────
     def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: This Active Text Variable saves the Clipboard to disk for later retrieval by a Query or Host Command. If the clipboard is empty, the temporary file is deleted so Restore Clipboard knows there shouldn't be a clipboard active.

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: If you do not specify a slot parameter then the clipboard is saved to a slot-less file. When it is restored the file is not deleted so you can do multiple identical clipboard restorations. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: If you do specify a slot parameter then you may save the clipboard to one of ten different clipboard slots (0-9). When you restore a clipboard slot, the clipboard file is deleted. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: You may specify a slot number of "PUSH" to perform a stack-based push operation (eg, `$SCB(PUSH)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $SCB$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$SCB(4)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text: _Kill Mouse Fields_

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$MKILL(x0,y0,x1,y1,inout)$`

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text:
```text
$MKILL(opt:X0, opt:Y0, opt:X1, opt:Y1, opt:INOUT)$

       opt:X0        opt:Y0
           ──            ──
           0-65535       0-65535
           ──            ──
       def=<none>    def=<none>

       opt:X1        opt:Y1         opt:INOUT
           ──            ──             ─────
           0-65535       0-65535        IN
           ──            ──             OUT
       def=<none>    def=<none>         ─────
                                    def=IN
```

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text: If no parameters are specified then all mouse fields currently defined are deleted (just like [RIP_KILL_MOUSE_FIELDS](4.2-mouse-fields-and-pointer.md#rip_kill_mouse_fields) does). If you specify the five parameters, you are defining a box on the screen that should have the mouse fields inside or outside of it deleted. Whether mouse fields inside the box or outside the box are destroyed depends on the INOUT parameter. If this parameter is specified as "IN" then all mouse fields inside the box are deleted. If the parameter is set to "OUT" then all mouse fields outside the box are deleted. Coordinates are specified in World coordinates. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text: This Active Text Variable deletes all defined Mouse Fields exactly like `RIP_KILL_MOUSE_FIELDS` does. The benefit is when the user clicks on a Mouse Fields or Button, the Mouse Fields are removed, but the graphics remain on the screen. The fields could be subsequently re-defined quickly and easily without having to re-transmit an identical menu over again.

requirements.heading: $MKILL$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$MKILL$` ... Kill all mouse fields defined **Example:** `$MKILL(0,0,639,100,IN)$` ... Kill all mouse fields inside the box (0,0) to (639,100). **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: _Restore Mouse Fields_

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$RMF(source)$`

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text:
```text
$RMF(opt:SOURCE)$
         ──────
         BASE
         POP
         0-9
         ──────
     def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: This Active Text Variable restores any Mouse Fields saved with [`$SMF$`](#smf). You may have only one set of mouse fields saved at once. If no mouse fields were saved, or if the number of fields saved is 0, then no mouse fields are active.

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified, then the non-slot specific mouse fields saved with a `$SMF$` command is restored (the saved mouse field file is not deleted). If a slot parameter is specified then the mouse fields saved with `$SMF(slot)$` is restored then the disk file is deleted. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot number of "POP" then you will be performing a stack-based pop operation (eg, `$RMF(POP)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: If you specify "BASE" instead of a slot number then you will be restoring the mouse fields from the mouse field data backup area's base save area. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: > **NOTE:** You may restore slot-less saved Mouse Fields more than once is you wish. In other words, if you do a `$SMF$` command, you may execute `$RMF$` one or more times. But if you do a `$SMF(1)$` you may only do a `$RMF(1)$` once. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $RMF$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RMF(4)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: _Save Mouse Fields_

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$SMF(destination)$`

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: **Syntax:**

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text:
```text
$SMF(opt:DESTINATION)$
         ───────────
         BASE
         PUSH
         0-9
         ───────────
     def=BASE
```

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: This Active Text Variable saves all defined Mouse Fields and Mouse Buttons to a temporary file for later retrieval. This is designed especially for the graphical designer who wishes to pop-up a dialog box on the screen with one or more mouse fields, and when finished, to restore the screen and original mouse fields. This command is intended to be used with the Restore Mouse Fields text variable [`$RMF$`](#rmf).

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: If no slot parameter is specified then the mouse field definitions will be stored to a non-slot specific file (similar to [`$SAVE$`](#save) with no parameter). This file can be restored multiple times. If you specify a slot, then the fields are stored to slot-specific files. When a saved mouse field definition in a particular slot is restored, the corresponding file is automatically deleted upon restoration. _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: If you specify a slot number of "PUSH" then you will be performing a stack-based push operation (eg, `$SMF(PUSH)$`). _(v2.A1)_

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: If you specify "BASE" instead of a slot number then you will be storing the mouse fields into the mouse field data backup area's base save area. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $SMF$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$SMF(4)$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $RESTORE$
requirements.text: _Restore a screen snapshot_

requirements.heading: $RESTORE$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$RESTORE([source])$`

requirements.heading: $RESTORE$
requirements.text: `source` is case-insensitive BASE (default), POP, or decimal 0..9. At most one argument is allowed. BASE restores the reusable screen base backup; POP restores/consumes the top screen-stack entry; a number restores that screen slot and then requests deletion. Protected numbered snapshots restore but survive deletion. Numeric deletion is requested **even after a failed restore**; POP consumes only after successful restoration.

requirements.heading: $RESTORE$
requirements.text: This restores physical screen pixels and the saved palette RGB into the **currently selected palette entry**. It changes no current port, viewport, graphics/button style, status-bar visibility or other data table. Palette-entry protection does not prevent that direct RGB overwrite. See the [exact screen capture/restore set, protection and lifetime](7.2-data-backup-areas.md#screen-save-area). For the eight-family composition use [`RESTOREALL`](#restoreall).

requirements.heading: $RESTORE$
requirements.text: **Example:** `$RESTORE(3)$` **Returns:** nothing
requirements.reason: Historical/contextual description, navigation, or illustrative action example. Concrete v3 capture/activation, alias and slot semantics are tracked in adjacent requirements; the legacy implementation is frozen unchanged.

requirements.heading: $RESTOREx$
requirements.text: _Restore numbered screen snapshot, x = 0..9_

requirements.heading: $RESTOREx$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$RESTORE0$` … `$RESTORE9$`

requirements.heading: $RESTOREx$
requirements.text: Each zero-argument alias performs exactly `RESTORE(x)`, including its current-palette binding, snapshot protection and delete-after-attempt behavior. RIPtel 3.1 registers **RESTORE0 as well as RESTORE1..9**. An argument to an alias is a variable error. The parameterized form is preferred for new content. These aliases do not restore extra viewport/style/status state or use a different RIPTERMx.SAV file contract.

requirements.text: **Example:** `$RESTORE3$` **Returns:** nothing

requirements.heading: $SAVE$
requirements.text: _Save a screen snapshot_

requirements.heading: $SAVE$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$SAVE([destination])$`

requirements.heading: $SAVE$
requirements.text: `destination` is case-insensitive BASE (default), PUSH, or decimal 0..9. At most one argument is allowed. BASE replaces the reusable screen base backup; PUSH adds a screen-stack entry; a number saves/replaces that slot unless its existing snapshot is protected.

requirements.heading: $SAVE$
requirements.text: The snapshot contains physical screen pixels from **port zero's screen DC** and current-palette RGB, with saved bitmap dimensions. It does **not** include viewports, current-port/palette selectors, graphics/button-style tables, status-bar visibility, mouse fields, text windows, offscreen contents or environments. Use [`SAVEALL`](#saveall) for the actual eight-family composition. The [screen save area](7.2-data-backup-areas.md#screen-save-area) defines exact binding, restore effects and private storage; RIPTERM*.SAV files are not required by the protocol.

requirements.heading: $BACKSTAT$
requirements.text: The "base" field is set to "0" if the base save area is not in use, or "1" if it is in use. The "stack" field is set to the number of entries that are currently saved on the stack ("0" if its empty). The "slots" field states how many entries are saved in the data save slots. The "free" field determines how many stack/slot areas are not in use (ie, how many more can hold data). The final ten entries "s0" through "s9" are set to "0" or "1" indicating if that specific data save slot is currently in use or not. If you add up the "stack" and "slots" value, you will get a total value of entries stored in the stack/slot system. If you add this total value up with the value of "free", then you get the maximum number of entries allowed to be saved in the stack/slot system (currently this should be set not exceed 10).

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: When you are referring to a copy operation that involves the entire data table, you use the keyword "TBL". When referring to the Base Data Save Area, the keyword "BASE" is used. A Data Save Slot number is specified with the letter "S" followed by the slot index number (eg, S0, S3, S5, etc). An actual data table entry number is specified simply as an actual number from 0 to the total number of entries in the data table minus one. _(v2.A3)_

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: You can also specify the source as POP to indicate that you are copying (popping) data from the stack to some other destination (TBL, BASE or S0-S9). If you specify only one destination location, then the contents of the stack are copied to that location, then the stack is "popped", which basically deletes the top item on the stack (the one that was just copied). If you have multiple destinations, then the stack item is copied to each of those locations, then it is finally deleted from the stack after all of the copy operations are complete. _(v2.A4)_

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: You cannot copy a data table over itself, and you cannot copy a data table entry on top of itself. All destination parameters are checked for validity before any actual copy operations are performed. If any of them fail a syntax check then the entire `$COPY$` expression is rejected as a syntax error. _(v2.A4)_
requirements.reason: Parsed COPY/BACKSTAT expressions now dispatch complete-table operations for bound actual palette and device-port objects. Whole-table multi-destination semantics are verified. Remaining type adapters, port cursor/query metadata, intra-table policies in #16, expansion/stream parsing and terminal routing remain pending; TW examples are not claimed as executed.

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: Our of all six data tables that have 36 separate entries, one of them doesn't permit direct copying from one entry to another within the same data table. That table is the drawing port table. The reason for this is because of how complicated the subject of performing port copying from one entry to another. Do you copy over just the graphical data, and if so, do you stretch it to fit in the destination port if the dimensions of the ports don't match? On the other hand do you duplicate the port definition entirely, potentially copying over the bitmap data? If so, how do you handle copying to port #0 which cannot be deleted or re-defined? With all of these complicated issues involved, it was decided not to allow for ports to be copied from one entry to another. Perhaps in the future we will allow for this kind of operation when more research on the issues can be performed. _(v2.A4)_
requirements.reason: PR #71 documentation answers are adopted at a9e0c2f490714d82a0827675ffbc074aa5ae00e6; implementation and independent expectations must now be reconciled. Previous blocker review: Upstream #16 must reconcile palette reset in-use status or contradictory port current/entry-copy descriptions before observable table/variable behavior can be completed.

requirements.heading: $COPY$
requirements.text: **Resident queries:** an individual text-window entry copy duplicates that window's resident-query string. Port resident queries are carried by **whole-port-table backup/restoration**, including the global floating query and each screen port's own query; this does not permit individual port-entry copies. The earlier draft sentence claiming individual drawing-port copies also copied queries was inconsistent with the prohibition above. Original save/restore consumers and independent query-string allocations confirm this scope; see the [derivation](../research/issue-16-table-lifecycle.md#final-native-family-reset-and-backup-checkpoint).

requirements.heading: Live-entry copy validation and protection
requirements.text: The shipped driver validates the source and **all destinations before any live-entry copy**. An undefined source, a protected destination, an invalid destination or a destination equal to the source rejects the entire expression without changing any destination. This applies when a protected destination occurs after an otherwise writable one in the list, and even when the protected destination is undefined. A protected source may be read and copied.

requirements.heading: Live-entry copy validation and protection
requirements.text: Successful copies mark the destination defined. Their protection result depends on the table:

requirements.text: | Table | Writable destination 1..35 | Destination 0 |

requirements.text: | PAL, STYLE, TW, ENV | Copy the source protection flag along with its definition | Copy contents/definition and clear protection |

requirements.heading: Live-entry copy validation and protection
requirements.text: | BUT | Copy contents/definition and **clear destination protection** | Copy contents/definition and clear protection |

requirements.heading: Live-entry copy validation and protection
requirements.text: For example, with defined protected PAL slot 5 and writable slots 6/8, `$COPY(PAL,5,6,8)$` copies both palettes and protects both destinations. If slot 7 is protected, `$COPY(PAL,5,6,7,8)$` changes **none** of 6/7/8. With BUT, the successful destinations remain unprotected. An undefined source fails before copying; it is not implicitly defaulted or defined.

requirements.heading: Live-entry copy validation and protection
requirements.text: This permission prevalidation does not guarantee rollback for later resource-allocation failures. In particular, the original text-window helper can complete the record copy with an empty resident-query pointer if allocating its independent query string fails. Its caller ignores individual copy-helper returns after prevalidation. Preserve that distinction when describing the original behavior. _Evidence: original callbacks/consumers and [80,982 native lifecycle checks](../research/issue-16-table-lifecycle.md)._

requirements.heading: $CUR$
requirements.text: | `STYLE` | Graphics style data table |
requirements.reason: The owned 36-record component stores raw drawing/background/fill colours, explicit device pen/fill attributes, classic font attributes and write mode. It requires a caller-supplied initial record, copies current attributes on first-use selection, validates edits atomically, enforces protection and snapshots every stored value/current index/metadata independently of the source lifetime. Public STYLE metadata and generic owned-snapshot COPY have nonfatal failure/recovery tests, including injected allocation failure; coherent independent RGB scenes exercise the stored attributes on all canvases. This is the resolved ordinary-attribute subset: bootstrap defaults, extended font state, full context ownership/activation and reset semantics remain pending under #3/#11/#12/#16/#24. No active terminal routing or complete STYLE context is claimed. CUR(STYLE) reads the component current index; CUR(STYLE,n) remains unsupported because its defaults/context activation are unresolved.

requirements.heading: $ISPROT$
requirements.text: This command returns a value indicating if the specified element in the desired data object is protected or not. If it is protected, then it returns a "1". "0" is returned if it is not protected. For a numeric slot, if the specified data object element is not in use (ie, not defined), then this command returns "-1". The shipped CUR branch directly tests current protection without this definition check; an undefined-but-current palette after reset can therefore return "0" through CUR while its numeric ISPROT query returns "-1" ([native derivation](../research/issue-16-table-lifecycle.md)). requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: _Query or replace a drawing port’s JPEG image style_

requirements.heading: $IMGSTYLE$
requirements.text: **Query:** `$IMGSTYLE$` or `$IMGSTYLE(port)$`
requirements.reason: The separate IMGSTYLE callback supports bare/current/named queries and decimal setters for screen/offscreen ports. Keywords are case-insensitive OR values, including duplicates; no keywords replaces flags with zero. Undefined/inactive targets return -1 without mutation/diagnostic; protected enabled targets query successfully and setters return no value without mutation/error. Valid setters temporarily select the target and restore the previous selection even on conversion failure. Queries convert the complete stored device boundaries through the live current WORLD, without subtracting the far increment. Independent literal replies, all keyword combinations, invalid parameters, state/selection recovery and every supported canvas are tested. Enclosing multi-action host expansion is a separate acceptance requirement.

requirements.heading: $OVERFLOW$
requirements.text: _Navigate column-system overflow pages_

requirements.heading: $OVERFLOW$
requirements.text: **Format:** `$OVERFLOW([article [,operation [,mode]]])$`

requirements.heading: $OVERFLOW$
requirements.text: The [column-system contract](3.1-column-text-system.md#pagination---overflow-and-resetoverflow) defines the complete argument and state table. Article is decimal 1..35 or CUR; omitted means selected article. Omitted operation or CUR returns an opaque saved-page filename (or `<NONE>`); PAGE returns the one-based display number. NEXT/PREV modify a zero-based current index and return an empty string on success. Their SETVERBOSE mode additionally notifies at a boundary, which aborts the surrounding evaluation before a following playback macro. QUERY is non-mutating; the shipped PREV,QUERY defect returns the filename for current+1. Numeric operation selects an already available zero-based index; RESET disables and clears one article’s paging state while retaining its column definitions. Global [`$RESET(OVERFLOW)$`](#reset) also removes all columns and selection. Overflow pages are generated lazily when text is rendered, not precomputed as a total page list.

requirements.heading: 5.2 Templates & Conditionals
requirements.text: Templates - the Host Command Language's mechanism for _building_ [host commands](5.0-host-commands.md) out of pieces, which the White Paper calls "a cookie-cutter approach to host commands," constructed from whichever buttons are selected and which are not. RIPtel 3.1 retains slot templates and adds a macro/conditional preprocessor (`<<NAME>>`, `<<IF>>…<<ELSE>>…<<ENDIF>>`). The original driver now establishes their processing order and shipped exceptions; inherited template examples below describe the intended design where the documented chaining defect prevents reliable shipped output.
